Large-dataset benchmarks: expression, storage and Viewer

Xuesong Wang

Source: vignettes/expression_backend_benchmark.Rmd
expression_backend_benchmark.Rmd

Scope and evidence

This article separates expression access, CRB persistence, server preparation, and browser rendering. Their timings have different boundaries and cannot be added into an overall Viewer speedup. For backend selection, sidecar portability and launching the demo, see Working with large datasets.

The first section reports the current real-data expression-backend benchmark. The sections after it are historical experiments, kept as recorded; they were not remeasured under that protocol. A passed regression suite does not establish a performance result.

All tables read the small, checked-in records under inst/extdata/benchmarks/. These records are included in installed packages; the figures are pre-drawn images. Rendering this article requires neither a large dataset nor a developer cache. Do not overwrite recorded experiments with a new run.

BPCells storage was removed in CerebroNexus 5.2.0 (see NEWS.md). The BPCells rows, figures and statements in this article are the measurements recorded while it was supported; they are kept unchanged as history and cannot be reproduced with the current version, which stores external expression only in H5 files.

Real-data expression backends (Scale run, 2026-10-18)

This study compares four ways to store the expression matrix: H5 with gzip level 6 (HDF5Array’s default, used by the exporter before 5.1.3), the same H5 file at gzip level 0, i.e. written without compression (the exportFromSeurat() default from 5.1.3; h5_compression_level changes it), BPCells, and embedded storage. In the tables and figures, h5_uncompressed is the gzip level 0 file. Two public datasets were used: the 10x mouse brain E18 matrix (1,306,127 cells, 27,998 genes, 2.6 billion nonzeros) and the PsychAD human prefrontal cortex HBCC matrix (1,486,324 cells, 34,176 genes, 6.1 billion nonzeros). Each source was measured at 1k, 10k, 50k, 100k, 300k and 500k cells and at its full size.

Every source, size and backend combination was built five times, and every build was opened in two fresh R processes, one thread each. All processes read the same cells and the same fixed 12-gene panel. Lazy reads were fully materialized inside the timer, and the values were checked against the source matrix afterwards; all 540 access processes matched. Embedded storage was measured up to 500k cells. The full matrices exceed its sparse-index limit, so there are no full-size embedded results.

The run is 20261018T101740Z-1ed063d363a0-scale, measured at commit 1ed063d3 on one Linux host (Intel i7-14700, 128 GB RAM, R 4.6.1, BPCells 0.3.1, HDF5Array 1.40.0). All 270 builds succeeded. The table below keeps the median of each measurement; the raw files of the run are not part of this repository.

scale <- read_tsv("expression-backends-scale-20261018.tsv")
full_size <- scale[scale$n_cells == max(scale$n_cells[scale$source == "mouse_brain_e18"]) |
  scale$n_cells == max(scale$n_cells[scale$source == "human_pfc_hbcc"]), ]
full_size$total_gib <- full_size$total_mib / 1024
knitr::kable(full_size[, c("source", "n_cells", "backend", "total_gib", "build_s",
  "startup_s", "rss_mib", "warmed_p50_s", "block_12gene_s")], digits = 3,
  row.names = FALSE)
source n_cells backend total_gib build_s startup_s rss_mib warmed_p50_s block_12gene_s
human_pfc_hbcc 1486324 bpcells 27.044 542.2 3.54 697 0.828 0.902
human_pfc_hbcc 1486324 h5 9.838 2096.0 6.73 868 0.055 0.641
human_pfc_hbcc 1486324 h5_uncompressed 69.006 634.8 6.56 868 0.036 0.572
mouse_brain_e18 1306127 bpcells 2.836 154.0 3.43 677 0.591 0.891
mouse_brain_e18 1306127 h5 3.614 526.7 5.72 838 0.034 0.338
mouse_brain_e18 1306127 h5_uncompressed 29.738 194.7 6.04 837 0.025 0.296

At full size, H5 at gzip level 0 builds about three times faster than H5 at level 6 and reads single genes a quarter to a third faster, but it needs about seven to eight times more disk. BPCells has the smallest memory after load and the fastest 12-gene reads on a shuffled 100k-cell subset, but a warmed full-cell single-gene read takes 0.6-0.8 s, against 0.02-0.06 s for H5. Embedded storage is competitive only for small datasets: at 500k cells its single-gene read takes 1.7-3.2 s and its memory after load is about 12-23 GiB.

Scale study. Medians across five builds against cell count (log10 axis); whiskers show the observed minimum and maximum. The dotted line and open symbols mark the full-size endpoint. a-b warmed single-gene read, c-d 12-gene block read, e-f memory after load, g-h total on-disk size.

Full-size endpoints of the same run. Small dots are single read processes (ten per backend) or builds (five per backend, panels g-h); the large symbol is the median across builds and the whisker the observed minimum and maximum.

The benchmark harness, the run’s summary tables and the figure code are in CerebroNexus_paper_code (benchmark/). The full-size figure uses the Scale run’s own full-size endpoints, not the separate Full run (20261017T174502Z-63d5337c3647-full). Timings come from one host and are not a guarantee for other hardware; the operating-system file cache was not cleared between processes.

Ren v2: expression backends

The recorded 2026-10-08 comparison used matching BPCells and HDF5 CRBs with 1,462,702 cells and 27,943 genes. Each backend ran in three fresh R processes, with alternating backend order. A separate planning process froze a 12-gene panel and reference value fingerprints. Every measurement verified identical single-row and block values outside the timed expressions.

startup_seconds includes source-package loading and CRB loading. First-gene latency is the first getter call in that process; repeated-gene latency is a within-process median. The 12-gene block is materialized. A fresh process does not imply a cold operating-system disk cache. These are R-side measurements, not time until a browser page becomes usable. The retained TSV does not contain a complete host/package manifest, limiting portability and exact environment reproduction; future reruns must retain it alongside their observations.

ren <- read_tsv("ren-backends-20261008.tsv")
stopifnot(all(ren$correctness == "OK"))
metrics <- c("startup_seconds", "first_gene_seconds", "hot_gene_p50_seconds", "twelve_gene_seconds")
ren_summary <- aggregate(ren[metrics], list(backend = ren$backend), stats::median)
knitr::kable(ren_summary, digits = 3)
backend startup_seconds first_gene_seconds hot_gene_p50_seconds twelve_gene_seconds
bpcells 15.393 1.884 0.929 1.209
h5 17.067 1.259 0.069 1.551

Historical Ren v2 comparison; medians of three fresh-process rounds. Backend computation, not browser page load.

On this workload, HDF5 has lower repeated single-gene latency, while BPCells has lower materialized block latency. This does not establish a universal backend ranking: storage orientation, query shape, data density and caching all matter. In particular, results from older BPCells layouts must not be used to describe the current gene-major layout without a matched rerun.

Historical mouse-million experiments

The input was the official 10x E18 mouse-brain matrix (1,306,127 barcodes, 27,998 features), reduced deterministically to one million evenly spaced cells. The preparation used a 50,000-cell sketch (seed 123), normalization, variable features, 30-component PCA, neighbors, clustering at resolution 1 and UMAP, then projected results to all selected cells. Counts used BPCells uint32 storage; thin RDS and qs2 CRBs reused the same sidecar.

The 2026-09-12 backend records used an Apple M1 Pro with 32 GiB RAM, macOS 27.0, R 4.6.1 arm64, BPCells 0.3.1 and Seurat 5.5.1. Exact source revisions and repeat counts are retained in million_cell_backend_hot_paths_manifest.tsv. The column named latest in that historical file refers to its recorded candidate 3fb88b8a, not the current checkout. Baselines are 69893a2b and 27303f21. The two baseline backend implementations were identical; their repeated columns are not independent experiments.

CRB lifecycle

Five alternating warm-cache rounds measured control-file size, writing, physical decoding and hydrated reading. Hydration includes sidecar attachment and canonical-cell checksum validation. It does not include browser rendering.

lifecycle <- utils::read.csv(file.path(records, "million_cell_crb_pr165.csv"))
knitr::kable(lifecycle[, c("candidate", "size_mib", "write_median_ms",
  "decode_median_ms", "hydrated_median_ms")], digits = 2)
candidate size_mib write_median_ms decode_median_ms hydrated_median_ms
pr165 26.83 8001 1296 1479
thin_rds 13.92 2947 93 356
thin_qs2 13.21 231 41 297

Server hot paths

Three warm-cache repetitions measured filtering, canonical indexing and expression reads, with equality checks before timing. Allocation describes R allocations, not browser heap or whole-process RSS. A recorded zero-millisecond value is below the timer resolution, not literally free computation.

hot <- read_tsv("million_cell_backend_hot_paths.tsv")
knitr::kable(hot[, c("metric", "scale", "pr165_ms", "latest_ms",
  "pr165_alloc_mib", "latest_alloc_mib", "check")], digits = 1)
metric scale pr165_ms latest_ms pr165_alloc_mib latest_alloc_mib check
full projection selection 1,000,000 cells; all groups; 100% 197 31 199.1 19.1 equal
filtered projection selection 1,000,000 cells; 17/33 clusters; 25% = 134557 329 28 166.5 39.5 equal
cell index resolution 1,000,000 shuffled canonical indices vs barcode match 79 0 27.1 0.0 equal
single-gene expression 1 gene x 1,000,000 cells; canonical indices; BPCells 4063 4022 154.1 157.1 equal
shuffled single-gene expression 1 gene x 100,000 shuffled cells; storage-order BPCells read 7886 5881 33.4 22.3 equal
RGB expression 3 genes x 1,000,000 cells; canonical indices; 3 reads vs 1 12498 4021 461.4 226.1 equal
multi-panel expression 9 genes x 1,000,000 cells; canonical indices; transpose removed 4309 4189 562.3 451.0 equal
mean expression 100 genes x 1,000,000 cells; canonical indices; backend-native 5912 3931 1916.8 65.4 equal

The accompanying million_cell_backend_bundle.tsv records historical Linked bundle construction and JSON costs; it predates later geometry/resource changes. Static HTTP geometry and metadata must be counted separately from WebSocket payloads. A tiny primary message is not the complete network cost.

Browser acceptance boundaries

Keep cold first entry, warm entry, revisit and repeated operations separate. Record draw submission, GPU completion, painted acknowledgement and progressive completion separately; global Shiny idle is not a substitute for page readiness. The request must match the current dataset generation, identity and selection. Use the same dataset, viewport, source revision, browser and initial state on both sides. Record timing and memory profiles in separate runs.

The historical five-round browser series and its immutable candidate/fixture identities are kept in CerebroNexus_paper_code under data/viewer_performance/million_cell_pages_pr4_pr5_4_6_3*. Those records used macOS Chrome and an older completion boundary for Linked Views. Later Windows Brave acceptance used WSL R, not Windows-native R. Neither series can be pooled with the other. Durable results and limitations are summarized in PR184_ACCEPTANCE.md in the same folder. Stable Gene first usability below three seconds has not been established, and there is no matched current-release, all-page speedup claim.

Earlier exploratory pilot

The 2026-07-30 embedded/BPCells/HDF5 sweep is retained in Git history under tests/bench/result/archive/pilot-2026-07-30/. It used real mouse-brain and human-PFC counts, synthetic grouping/embeddings, and contiguous cell blocks. The macOS arm64 host had 32 GB RAM. The run preceded balanced independent repeats and complete provenance; its tables and figures are exploratory.

Its useful lesson is that dense realization and construction of a large in-memory Seurat object can dominate memory before a backend is written. Cell count alone is not a memory budget: density and nonzero count matter. Do not generalize its approximately 53 bytes/nonzero peak or old backend ranking to current streaming exports. Raw pilot CSVs remain available for inspection; current figure scripts intentionally require validated repeated runs instead of treating this pilot as release evidence.

Reproduce figures and rerun measurements

The figure code and every measurement script are in CerebroNexus_paper_code: viewer/ holds the Viewer, CRB and Ren diagnostics and the Ren figure (viewer/scripts/plot_ren_backend_acceptance.R), and benchmark/ holds the repeated H5 / BPCells / embedded experiment. They run against a CerebroNexus checkout and need its declared dependencies and enough storage; they do not work from an installed package alone. Record git rev-parse HEAD, sessionInfo(), host/browser versions and artifact checksums with every new output, and save new runs outside the recorded-data directory.

The million-cell and Ren demo data used by run-demo.R are prepared by the scripts in data-raw/large-demo/ of a CerebroNexus checkout. For the mouse preparation, allow at least 16 GiB free disk for the recorded artifact layout, additional space for parallel backends/outputs, and tens of minutes or longer depending on hardware and downloads. The source alone is about 3.93 GiB. Full Ren preparation has separate large download/storage costs; inspect the preparation script and available disk before starting it. Do not use an arbitrary memory limit or a historical completion time as a guarantee.

source("data-raw/large-demo/h5_transposed_write.R")
source("data-raw/large-demo/prepare_viewer_1m_data.R")
pkgload::load_all(".")
crb <- prepareViewer1mBenchmarkData()

Preserve raw rounds, source identities, failed observations and limits; never replace them with a single favorable timing.
